items.title: 53279_Lee Young Oral History Interview
items.q: Cootie Williams traveled with us when I was a little kid on the carnival

ctx.x: used to talk about -- what was that man's name? Clarence Williams. My father taught Clarence Williams, and I think you'd have to go back a ways to see who this was, but he was a pianist, and I've since -- I read of him, you know, but he was -- I don't know when, it must've been in the 20's or in the 18's or something. A little research on it would probably get him ... but he -- my dad taught him.

He also taught Cootie Williams. Cootie Williams traveled with us when I was a little kid on the carnival -- we used to go on carnivals, and Cootie, it seems to me that my dad got him in Birmingham or Mobile, Alabama. We were with a carnival called "Lackman and Carson Show". That's when the carnivals used to have a railroad car; they would have the Pullman cars and they would have dining cars, and you used to travel just as the circuses did.
And we had one of the shows on the carnival. And Lester and my sister and my mother and my dad - Lester and my sister played in the band; my sister also played saxaphone, Irma.
